claim: Plasma 6.7 (16 June 2026) adds per-screen virtual desktops, simultaneous ICC colour management plus HDR, and performance/power improvements.
quote: After 21 years, hopefully it will have been worth the wait… per-screen virtual desktops have finally arrived! ... No longer do you have to choose between color management using an ICC profile or enjoying HDR content; now both are possible at the same time!

claim: KDE is effectively the only desktop with a working GlobalShortcuts portal backend; GNOME 50 has none functional and xdg-desktop-portal-wlr ships no implementation.
quote: KDE is currently the only desktop environment with support for global shortcuts

claim: GNOME extension review runs through a single reviewer; in spring 2026 the queue reached nearly 500 pending submissions, many just metadata bumps for GNOME 50 compatibility.
quote: the review queue is currently nearing 500 ... Every extension is looked at by a single person.

claim: Linux Mint 23 (due end of 2026) fully supports both X11 and Wayland; Mint has not committed to making Wayland the default.
quote: Both X11 and Wayland will be fully supported ... wants the option 'on the table' without committing to a timeline for the switch.

claim: Plasma 6.8 (expected 14 Oct 2026) drops the dedicated X11 session; Plasma 6.7 is the last with one, and the X11 session is maintained only until early 2027.
quote: Plasma 6.7 is the last version expected to ship with a dedicated X11 session ... From Plasma 6.8 in October 2026, only Wayland will be available at login; X11 apps will still run via XWayland.

claim: GNOME 50 removed the X11 session entirely (about 27,540 lines cut from Mutter); you cannot log into an X11 GNOME session even with Xorg installed, though X11 apps still run under XWayland.
quote: Mutter scrapped 27,540 lines of X11 code as the team went all-in on Wayland. You can't log into GNOME 50 using X11 as the display server, locally or remotely, even if you manually install X.org.

claim: Cinnamon's Wayland session is no longer considered experimental in the next release; Mint developers describe it as almost on par with X11.
quote: We worked really hard on Wayland and we got to the point where it feels solid and the experience is almost on par with X11.

claim: Xfce's Wayland compositor xfwl4 reached first preview on 22 June 2026 after roughly six months of development and still has bugs and missing features.
quote: announced by longtime Xfce developer Brian Tarricone on June 22, 2026, stating it is ready for wider testing after nearly six months of development

claim: Xfce's Wayland roadmap does not target X11 feature parity for the 4.22 release; both xfwm4 and xfwl4 will ship so X11 and Wayland sessions both remain available.
quote: For Xfce 4.22, the stabilization work continues, reaching X11 feature parity is not yet the target

claim: COSMIC 1.0 shipped 11 December 2025 alongside Pop!_OS 24.04 LTS as System76's Wayland-only Rust desktop, with per-workspace tiling, placement hints and persistent layouts; 1.0.x releases cleaned up NVIDIA explicit-sync and XWayland fractional-scaling issues.
quote: COSMIC 1.0 shipped alongside Pop!_OS 24.04 LTS on December 11, 2025, marking the first stable version of its fully Rust based COSMIC desktop environment.

claim: Ubuntu 26.04 LTS (April 2026) moves GNOME to Wayland-only and removes the Xorg session option while keeping X11 apps working via XWayland.
quote: Ubuntu 26.04 LTS moves the GNOME desktop to Wayland-only and removes the Xorg session option while keeping X11 applications runnable via Xwayland.

claim: Ubuntu users are actively seeking advice because 26.04 drops X11 session support.
quote: I need some advice now that Ubuntu is dropping support for x11 in 26.04

claim: KDE metrics show over 95% of Plasma 6.6 users running Wayland, and Plasma 6.7 is the last release with X11 session support.
quote: Over 95% of Plasma 6.6 users are running on Wayland

claim: KDE Plasma is the desktop most commonly recommended to Windows 10/11 switchers because its default layout preserves Windows muscle memory with only small tweaks.
quote: KDE Plasma is already pretty much the perfect desktop environment for those switching from Windows 10 or 11, but a few tweaks make everything run much more smoothly.

claim: 2026 idle memory measurements rank XFCE/LXQt lightest (~1.36 GB), then Cinnamon (~1.89 GB), GNOME (~2.10 GB) and KDE Plasma (~2.67 GB) of total system usage.
quote: XFCE and LXQt demonstrate the lowest memory footprint with usage between 1,360-1,370 MiB, significantly lower than GNOME (2,100 MiB) and KDE Plasma (2,670 MiB).

claim: KDE exposes configurable three- and four-finger touchpad gesture bindings in System Settings on Wayland.
quote: You can bind three-finger and four-finger swipes to actions like switching desktops, toggling Present Windows, or opening the application launcher.

claim: GNOME 50 enables fractional scaling and VRR by default, improves NVIDIA performance, and gives Remote Desktop Vulkan/VA-API acceleration, HiDPI-aware scaling, camera redirection and Kerberos auth.
quote: For users with compatible monitors, VRR provides a tear-free experience where the display's refresh rate matches the application's frame rate

claim: GNOME supports three-finger swipe workspace switching and Activities overview gestures out of the box on Wayland with no extra software.
quote: GNOME 40+ ... supports three-finger swipe gestures for workspace switching out of the box on Wayland with no extra software needed.

claim: Cinnamon 6.8 adds proper window/menu mapping, focus-stealing prevention, improved multi-monitor support, hardware acceleration and full HiDPI to its Wayland session.
quote: The improvements include proper mapping for new windows/menus, proper focus stealing prevention, addressing Wayland crash scenarios, improved multi-monitor support, hardware acceleration improvements, full HiDPI, window progress, and session fixes.

claim: Feature matrix: GNOME and KDE Plasma support HDR and VRR while Xfce and Cinnamon support neither; per-DE RAM measurements with base-system overhead subtracted put GNOME, Plasma, Xfce and Cinnamon within roughly 60 MB of each other.
quote: KDE Plasma: 347 MB / GNOME: 408 MB / Xfce: 394 MB / Cinnamon: 348 MB

claim: On Sway in January 2026: single-window screen sharing is broken, XWayland is not scaled (blurry X11 apps), Chrome's GPU process dies after resize, and DisplayPort MST tiled monitors appear as two screens.
quote: I cannot share a specific window (the entire monitor shows up as a single window) ... Sway does not support scaling with Xwayland

claim: Comparison of tiling compositors in 2026: niri best for laptop-first scrollable workflows, Sway most predictable and lowest overhead, Hyprland best eye candy with faster churn and rough edges.
quote: Niri is recommended as the best overall Wayland tiling manager for laptop-first workflows ... Hyprland is best if you want modern eye candy and dynamic tiling but accept faster-churn development and occasional rough edges.

claim: niri arranges windows in an infinite horizontal scrolling strip per workspace rather than a split grid.
quote: windows are arranged in an infinite horizontal scrolling strip per workspace, with new windows appearing to the right

claim: Electron apps such as Slack, Element and Jitsi show a redundant duplicate screen-share picker on Wayland, and PipeWire capture may need the WebRTCPipeWireCapturer feature flag.
quote: Redundant app-created screen share dialog on Linux Wayland

claim: On Wayland, Zoom's first screen share works but a second share attempt produces a black screen.
quote: The first time sharing a screen works fine, but if you stop sharing and try to share again, it only shares a completely black window or screen.

claim: The GlobalShortcuts portal is the sanctioned Wayland replacement for direct key grabbing, letting apps register shortcuts that fire regardless of focus.
quote: The Global Shortcuts portal lets applications create global shortcuts sessions, and register shortcuts to them, with these shortcuts being activated regardless of focus state.

claim: Generic clipboard managers on Wayland cannot monitor clipboard changes while unfocused; they only see XWayland windows or changes while focused.
quote: Clipboard managers cannot monitor clipboard events when running unfocused on Wayland, only detecting clipboard changes from Xwayland windows or when the application has active focus

claim: KRDP shares only an already-logged-in Plasma session and does not support headless sessions with no plans to; GNOME/GDM supports remote login and headless sessions.
quote: KRDP does not support headless sessions and there are no immediate plans to do so in the future. While GDM allows you to have remote login and headless sessions, with SDDM you're locked out for the moment

claim: Working explicit sync on NVIDIA requires Xwayland 24.1+, a compositor with explicit-sync support (KWin 6.1+) and NVIDIA drivers 555.58 or newer.
quote: proper support requires Xwayland 24.1+, a compositor supporting explicit sync (kwin 6.1+), and NVIDIA drivers 555.58+

claim: Users report freezes on NVIDIA 580-series drivers under KDE Plasma Wayland, where the screen blanks and the video output stays frozen.
quote: NVIDIA 580 on KDE wayland freezes

claim: HN discussion in 2026: GNOME and Plasma Wayland are reported trouble-free on AMD/Intel, while remaining complaints cluster around NVIDIA, Wine multi-display pointer bugs and per-compositor fragmentation.
quote: I've been using wayland with Gnome for years without a single issue ... Wine apps will randomly have pointer location issues if you run multiple displays

claim: Plasma 6.6.4 was still fixing fractional-scaling artefacts under Wayland including pixelated window buttons, missing menu shadows and detached tooltip shadows.
quote: Oxygen resolves pixelated window buttons, missing menu shadows, detached tooltip shadows on fractional scaling under Wayland, and panel theme issues.

claim: KWin implements the experimental xx-fractional-scale-v2 Wayland protocol for pixel-level positioning, eliminating gaps between windows on high-density displays.
quote: KWin implements Wayland's experimental xx-fractional-scale-v2 protocol to achieve pixel-level positioning and eliminate gaps between windows on high-density displays.
